title: Big questions
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

allowedPatterns: Für mich + ist + <abstraktes Nomen> + wichtiger + als + <Nomen>

rules.text: THE zu-INFINITIVE, THE CLAUSE TYPE ABSTRACT TALK CANNOT BE DONE WITHOUT. Es ist schwer, das zu verstehen: comma, then the clause, then zu immediately before the infinitive, and nothing after it. The infinitive is the last word of the sentence. L3-M1 taught one member of this family — the purpose clause um … zu — and the infixed zu of separable verbs, einzukaufen, aufzustehen. The plain zu plus a simple infinitive is new here, and it is what carries every sentence in this module.

A MODAL VERB TAKES NO zu, AND THIS IS THE ERROR AN ENGLISH SPEAKER MAKES. Ich muss gehen, Ich kann das verstehen, Ich will nichts sagen — no comma, no zu, infinitive at the end. English puts to after almost everything (I need TO go, I want TO understand), so the hand reaches for it. The rule is short: after müssen, können, wollen, sollen, dürfen and mögen the infinitive stands bare.

glauben IS HEAVIER THAN believe. An anglophone hedges every abstract claim with I believe, and German glauben leans towards religious belief in a way English believe does not. The ordinary hedge for a position is Ich finde or Ich bin davon überzeugt, both already yours from L1-M9 and L4-M4. Keep glauben for what you actually take on faith, and the sentence stops sounding like a confession.

EVERY zu-INFINITIVE HERE IS ONE UNIT, AND THE INDEX IS WHY. The bare zu already belongs to L1-M8, where it is the TOO of Das ist zu teuer — an entirely different word. So zu sein, zu sagen, zu verstehen are each learned and tapped whole. Read them as one piece and you will never write the too by accident.

TWO WORDS THIS MODULE WANTS AND CANNOT HAVE. Würde, dignity, is spelled identically to the unreal auxiliary würde of L3-M4 once the index folds the capital away, so this course writes Menschenwürde instead — one word, and a better one anyway. Der Glaube, faith, folds onto L1-M9's glaube, I think, so the noun here is Überzeugung, conviction. Neither is a workaround you have to remember: both are what a careful German writer would pick.

STATING A POSITION IS NOT SUSTAINING ONE. This module hands you the nouns and the clause type, and it stops there: name a value, say what it is worth to you, ask what it means to someone else. Holding a position against objections — conceding, distinguishing, coming back — is L5-M6, one rung on. An argument built here would be an argument taken from there.

sentences.display: Für mich ist Freiheit wichtiger als Geld.
sentences.cue: For me, freedom matters more than money.
sentences.literal: For me is freedom more-important than money.

words.note: Feminine, die Freiheit. Every -heit noun is feminine, which is the one gender rule in this module you can rely on without looking.
The comparative of L3-M2's wichtig, first taught there as the plain adjective. German compares with -er and then als, where English switches to more.

sentences.trap: English needs more for a long adjective — more important — and German never does: wichtig becomes wichtiger, interessant becomes interessanter. Writing mehr wichtig is the single most common English-shaped error in an abstract sentence.
sentences.sound: fuer mikh ist FRY-hyt VIKH-tig-er als GELT — Freiheit is two clear diphthongs, and the -er of wichtiger is a swallowed uh.

variations.display: Für mich ist Gerechtigkeit wichtiger als Geld.
variations.cue: For me, justice matters more than money.
variations.changed: The value in the slot changes and nothing else moves — this frame is how the module states a position without arguing for it.

mistake.display: Für mich ist Freiheit mehr wichtig als Geld
mistake.why: German has no more plus adjective. The comparative is built on the word itself: wichtiger. mehr is only for quantities — mehr Geld, mehr Zeit.

sentences.usage: Putting a value on the table as yours, at the start of a conversation rather than at the end of an argument.
sentences.mnemonic: Für mich marks it as a position, not a fact — the two words that make an abstract claim safe to make.

sentences.display: Es ist wichtig, immer ehrlich zu sein.
sentences.cue: It is important to always be honest.
sentences.literal: It is important, always honest to be.

words.note: The frame that opens a zu-clause. es is a placeholder for the clause after the comma, and the comma is compulsory in German.
Learned as one unit, because bare zu is already L1-M8's word for too. zu goes immediately in front of the infinitive and nothing follows it.

sentences.trap: English lets the infinitive sit next to the adjective: important to be honest. German pushes it to the very end behind a comma, so everything you want to say has to be lined up before zu sein arrives.
sentences.sound: es ist VIKH-tikh, IM-er AIR-likh tsoo ZYN — the voice pauses at the comma, which is the audible half of the rule.

variations.display: Es ist wichtig, ehrlich zu sein.
variations.cue: It is important to be honest.
variations.changed: immer drops out. The clause is at its shortest here, which is the shape worth memorising before you start filling it.

mistake.display: Es ist wichtig zu immer ehrlich sein
mistake.why: Two rules broken at once: the comma is missing and zu has been parked at the front. zu belongs immediately before the infinitive, and the infinitive ends the sentence.

sentences.usage: Stating a general principle rather than a preference — the impersonal es keeps you out of it.
sentences.mnemonic: Comma, then everything, then zu and the verb — the zu is the last thing before the last thing.

sentences.display: Es ist schwer, Menschen wirklich zu verstehen.
sentences.cue: It is hard to really understand people.
sentences.literal: It is hard, people really to understand.

words.note: Masculine, der Mensch, and it takes -en in almost every other slot: den Menschen, die Menschen. It means a person as a species member, where Leute means a crowd.
One unit again, on L5-M1's verstehen. Whatever is being understood — Menschen here — stands in front of it, not after.

sentences.trap: An English speaker puts the object after the verb and runs out of sentence: to understand people really. German has already spent the end of the sentence on zu verstehen, so the object and the adverb both go in front of it.
sentences.sound: es ist SHVAIR, MEN-shen VEER-likh tsoo fer-SHTAY-en — verstehen carries its stress on the -steh-, and the ver- almost disappears.

variations.display: Es ist nicht leicht, Menschen zu verstehen.
variations.cue: It is not easy to understand people.
variations.changed: Understated instead of blunt: German prefers nicht leicht where English would say hard, and it softens the claim without hedging it.

mistake.display: Es ist schwer zu verstehen Menschen wirklich
mistake.why: English word order imported whole. Nothing may follow the infinitive: the object and the adverb go between the comma and zu.

sentences.usage: Conceding a difficulty in a conversation about people, without making it about anyone present.
sentences.mnemonic: Everything queues before zu — the infinitive locks the door on the way out.

sentences.display: Ich bin davon überzeugt, dass Gerechtigkeit möglich ist.
sentences.cue: I am convinced that justice is possible.
sentences.literal: I am there-of convinced, that justice possible is.

words.note: Feminine, die Gerechtigkeit, built on recht. Every -keit noun is feminine, the same rule as -heit and just as reliable.
From mögen, to like or may. It stands at the end of a dass-clause in front of the verb, exactly where an adjective belongs there.

sentences.trap: Reaching for Ich glaube here is the module's central interference. glauben leans towards faith; Ich bin davon überzeugt is what a German says about a position they can defend, and it is the honest hedge for an abstract claim.
sentences.sound: ikh bin da-FON ue-ber-TSOYKT, das guh-REKH-tikh-kyt MUERK-likh ist — davon puts its stress on the second syllable, which is what marks it as pointing forward.

variations.display: Ich bin davon überzeugt, dass Freiheit möglich ist.
variations.cue: I am convinced that freedom is possible.
variations.changed: Only the abstract noun in the dass-clause moves; davon still points forward at the clause, which is its whole job.

mistake.display: Ich bin davon überzeugt, dass Gerechtigkeit ist möglich
mistake.why: dass sends the verb to the end. ist goes behind möglich, not in front of it — the same rule weil and denn already taught you.

sentences.usage: Stating a belief you would defend, as distinct from one you merely hold.
sentences.mnemonic: davon points forward at the dass-clause: convinced OF the thing that is about to arrive.

sentences.cue: What does responsibility mean to you?

words.note: Feminine, die Verantwortung, built on Antwort — the thing you have to answer for. Every -ung noun is feminine too.

sentences.trap: English asks what something means TO you; German asks für dich, with für plus the accusative. bedeuten needs no preposition of its own and takes the thing meant straight.
sentences.sound: vas buh-DOY-tet fer-ANT-vor-toong fuer dikh — Verantwortung stresses the -ant-, and the -ung ending is a soft oong.

variations.cue: What does freedom mean to you?
variations.changed: The abstract noun in the slot changes. This is the module's one question shape, and it is what turns a statement of values into a conversation.

mistake.why: zu is not the preposition here — and this zu would read as L1-M8's too as well. The phrase is für dich, and it is fixed.

sentences.usage: Handing the subject to the other person after you have stated your own position.
sentences.mnemonic: Verantwortung holds Antwort: it is what you will have to answer for.

sentences.display: Ohne Vertrauen gibt es keine Gesellschaft.
sentences.cue: Without trust there is no society.
sentences.literal: Without trust gives it no society.

words.note: Always takes the accusative and never an article after an abstract noun: ohne Vertrauen, ohne Hoffnung. It is the negative twin of mit.
Neuter, das Vertrauen — a verb turned into a noun, which is why it is capitalised and has no plural.
Feminine, die Gesellschaft. It also means company in the sense of people around you, which is where the abstract sense came from.

sentences.trap: es gibt is fixed and impersonal: there is, there are, both of them. The noun after it is accusative, which is why keine and not keiner, even though it looks like the subject in English.
sentences.sound: OH-nuh fer-TROW-en gipt es KY-nuh guh-ZEL-shaft — ohne has a long open o, and Vertrauen's -trau- is the ow of now.

variations.display: Ohne Vertrauen gibt es keine Freiheit.
variations.cue: Without trust there is no freedom.
variations.changed: The second abstract noun changes. Both slots take a bare noun with no article, which is what makes this frame sound like a maxim.

mistake.display: Ohne das Vertrauen gibt es keine Gesellschaft
mistake.why: Abstract nouns in this frame stand bare. das Vertrauen would mean a specific trust between named people, which turns a general claim into a report.

sentences.usage: Stating a general truth as a maxim, where naming who is involved would weaken it.
sentences.mnemonic: ohne takes nothing with it — no article, and the accusative behind it.

sentences.display: Was ist der Sinn des Lebens?
sentences.cue: What is the meaning of life?
sentences.literal: What is the meaning of-the life?

words.note: Three words, learned whole: der Sinn is masculine and des Lebens is L3-M8's genitive. Lebens is the genitive of das Leben and is not taught apart from this phrase.

sentences.trap: English can say life's meaning or the meaning of life. German only has the genitive here, and it goes behind: Sinn first, des Lebens after. The order never reverses.
sentences.sound: vas ist dair ZIN des LAY-bens — Sinn is short and clipped, Lebens has a long a, and the whole phrase runs as one word.

variations.display: Was ist der Sinn des Lebens für dich?
variations.cue: What is the meaning of life to you?
variations.changed: für dich hangs on the end and turns the largest question there is into one somebody can actually answer.

mistake.display: Was ist der Sinn von das Leben?
mistake.why: von plus dative works for many possessives and not for this one: the phrase is fixed as des Lebens. And after von it would have to be dem, never das.

sentences.usage: Asked half seriously, which is the only way it is ever asked.
sentences.mnemonic: Sinn des Lebens is one lump of German — take it whole and the genitive comes free.

sentences.display: Die Wahrheit ist manchmal schwer zu sagen.
sentences.cue: The truth is sometimes hard to say.
sentences.literal: The truth is sometimes hard to say.

words.note: Feminine, die Wahrheit, on wahr, true. The third -heit noun in this module, and the gender rule has not failed yet.
One unit on L2-M10's sagen. With schwer or leicht in front of it, no comma is needed — the clause is too short to take one.

sentences.trap: This is the one zu-clause with no comma, because it has no clause of its own: schwer zu sagen is a two-word tail on the adjective. Add an object and the comma comes back — es ist schwer, die Wahrheit zu sagen.
sentences.sound: dee VAAR-hyt ist MANKH-maal shvair tsoo ZAA-gen — Wahrheit's ah is long, and manchmal has the soft ch.

variations.display: Die Wahrheit ist manchmal schwer zu verstehen.
variations.cue: The truth is sometimes hard to understand.
variations.changed: A different infinitive in the same tail. Both are learned whole, which is why swapping them costs nothing.

mistake.display: Die Wahrheit ist manchmal schwer sagen
mistake.why: The infinitive after an adjective is not bare — that is the modal rule, and schwer is not a modal. It needs zu: schwer zu sagen.

sentences.usage: Softening what you are about to say, or explaining why you did not say it.
sentences.mnemonic: schwer zu sagen — short tail, no comma; give it an object and the comma is back.

sentences.display: Für mich ist die Menschenwürde keine Meinung, sondern ein Wert.
sentences.cue: For me, human dignity is not an opinion but a value.
sentences.literal: For me is the human-dignity no opinion, but-rather a value.

words.note: Feminine, die Menschenwürde — one word, Mensch plus Würde. This course writes the compound, because bare Würde is spelled like L3-M4's würde.
Masculine, der Wert. The plural die Werte is what people mean by their values; the singular can also be a price or a measurement.

sentences.trap: sondern, not aber. German splits the English but in two: sondern corrects a negative (not this, but that), aber adds a contrast. After keine the word can only be sondern.
sentences.sound: fuer mikh ist dee MEN-shen-vuer-duh KY-nuh MY-noong, ZON-dern eyn VAIRT — Menschenwürde stresses Men-, and the ü in -würde is long.

variations.display: Für mich ist die Menschenwürde ein Wert.
variations.cue: For me, human dignity is a value.
variations.changed: The negative half drops away and sondern goes with it — with nothing to correct, the sentence is a plain claim.

mistake.display: Für mich ist die Menschenwürde keine Meinung, aber ein Wert
mistake.why: aber cannot follow a negative it is correcting. keine … sondern is the pair; keine … aber leaves the correction hanging.

sentences.usage: Marking that something is not up for negotiation, without raising your voice about it.
sentences.mnemonic: sondern comes after a no; aber comes after a yes.

sentences.display: Ohne Hoffnung und Überzeugung ist das Leben schwer.
sentences.cue: Without hope and conviction, life is hard.
sentences.literal: Without hope and conviction is the life hard.

words.note: Feminine, die Hoffnung, on hoffen. Like Verantwortung it is an -ung noun, so the gender comes free.
Feminine, die Überzeugung, the noun of L4-M4's überzeugt. It is what this course uses where English would say faith or belief.
Neuter, das Leben, and the plural is identical. A verb turned noun again, which is why it is capitalised.

sentences.trap: Starting a German sentence with a long phrase pushes the verb to second position and the subject behind it: ist das Leben, not das Leben ist. English keeps the subject first and an anglophone forgets the swap exactly when the opening phrase is longest.
sentences.sound: OH-nuh HOF-noong oont ue-ber-TSOY-goong ist das LAY-ben shvair — Überzeugung opens on a long ü and stresses the -zeu-.

variations.display: Ohne Hoffnung ist das Leben sehr schwer.
variations.cue: Without hope, life is very hard.
variations.changed: One noun instead of two and sehr added — the same inversion, at the shortest length where the swap still has to happen.

mistake.display: Ohne Hoffnung und Überzeugung das Leben ist schwer
mistake.why: The verb must be the second element. With the ohne phrase in first position, ist comes next and das Leben follows it.

sentences.usage: Closing a serious conversation with something general, which is what German does instead of an ending.
sentences.mnemonic: Long opener, verb second, subject third — the phrase took the first seat, so the subject moves back.
